why: Paragraph 169 names the object 'a small dog lash.'

text: That afternoon: Holmes's eye is caught by a small dog lash on the bed, tied in a loop
why: Holmes and Watson reached Stoke Moran in the afternoon (¶116–169), and the lash is found during that visit.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for?
why: A plain question about the object the story has just shown, with the loop given as the reason to ask.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for? — a noose for handling a creature he dare not touch
id: q.why_lash=a noose for handling a creature he dare not touch
why: The story has established a cheetah and baboon that villagers fear (¶27, ¶48), so a noose for handling a dangerous creature is a possibility a reader could reasonably consider.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for? — to hold or lead a dog or one of his larger animals
id: q.why_lash=to hold or lead a dog or one of his larger animals
why: A dog lash is a leash-type object, and the household keeps a cheetah and baboon that roam the grounds (¶27), so holding or leading an animal is a fair possibility.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for? — a noose to use on a person
id: q.why_lash=a noose to use on a person
why: Roylott is violent and has bent a poker and hurled a blacksmith (¶26–27, ¶110), so a person-directed noose is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for? — a way of hanging it up, or a makeshift repair
id: q.why_lash=a way of hanging it up, or a makeshift repair
why: Nothing in the story suggests the lash is broken or needs repair, and no earlier detail makes hanging it up or a makeshift repair a live possibility.

text: What is the small dog lash tied into a loop for? — it is curled upon itself and tied so as to make a loop of whipcord
